I'll read both files now.Let me read the rest of the findings file.Based on my complete review of both files, I checked every concrete claim against the findings. The section is overwhelmingly faithful, with numeric values, locations, and study results matching their cited findings. I found one attribution problem.

The sentence: *"Indian pilot areas recorded rice-yield increases of 30--120\% and average increases of 54--136\% across crops, with cost--benefit ratios of 2.5--4.6 and payback periods of 2--3 years \parencite{Satyanarayana2007}"* — the "30–120%" rice figure, the "2.5–4.6" cost-benefit ratio, and "2–3 years" payback all correctly come from Satyanarayana2007 (findings lines 89, 91). However, the inserted figure "average increases of 54--136% across crops" is not in any Satyanarayana2007 finding; it matches Ritzema2011 exactly ("crop yields increased on average 54% for sugarcane, 64% for cotton, 69% for rice, and 136% for wheat" — line 112). That specific statistic is attributed to the wrong paper.
